originalGroup.material:
The puppet with a long nose

Our class made puppets for a short play. Mine was an old man with a hat and a very long paper nose. I thought the nose was the funniest part. ____1____ The audience would see it before they heard his first line.

At rehearsal, the nose caught on the edge of the little stage. I tried to lift the puppet higher. ____2____ He seemed to be looking at the ceiling instead of at the other character.

Our teacher asked me to try a shorter nose. I was disappointed, but I made one from spare paper. ____3____ This time, I could turn the puppet without catching it on anything.

My friend said the old man's voice was funny too. I practised saying the line slowly, then very quickly. ____4____ The slower version gave everyone time to understand why he was confused.

At the show, people laughed at the right moment. They did not know about the first nose. I kept both versions in my art folder afterwards. ____5____ The final puppet had become more enjoyable because I could use it well.

A sign by the small gate

Our school garden has two gates. Visitors usually find the large one first, but it is kept closed during gardening lessons. We enter through the smaller gate beside the shed. ____1____ A new visitor could easily wait at the wrong place.

I offered to make a sign. My first message said only "Come this way". I put it beside the large gate and showed it to a friend. ____2____ From where she stood, the words gave no direction at all.

We added an arrow and the words "Small gate beside the shed". The teacher checked the route before we put it up. ____3____ A sign should not send people along a path that is blocked.

On Friday, I watched a visitor stop at the large gate, read the sign and walk towards the shed. ____4____ I still asked whether she needed help, but she said she had found the way.

The sign was taken down after the lesson because the entry arrangement could change on other days. ____5____ We kept it in the garden cupboard for the next time the same route was used.

A sign by the small gate

Our school garden has two gates. Visitors usually find the large one first, but it is kept closed during gardening lessons. We enter through the smaller gate beside the shed. ____1____ A new visitor could easily wait at the wrong place.

I offered to make a sign. My first message said only "Come this way". I put it beside the large gate and showed it to a friend. ____2____ From where she stood, the words gave no direction at all.

We added an arrow and the words "Small gate beside the shed". The teacher checked the route before we put it up. ____3____ A sign should not send people along a path that is blocked.

On Friday, I watched a visitor stop at the large gate, read the sign and walk towards the shed. ____4____ I still asked whether she needed help, but she said she had found the way.

The sign was taken down after the lesson because the entry arrangement could change on other days. ____5____ We kept it in the garden cupboard for the next time the same route was used.
questions.explanation: E contrasts familiar pupils with new visitors, developed by wrong-place risk. B unclear message/D path check/A successful visitor/F temporary sign fit later; C contradicts gate closure.
questions.hint: Use the complete material and the question together.

options.text: A. This time, the arrow led her to the correct entrance.
B. She asked which way I meant.
C. Both gates were always open throughout every lesson.
D. We checked that the space beside the shed was clear.
E. That difference was obvious to us, but not to everyone.
F. We did not want a temporary instruction to look permanent.

originalGroup.material:
Drawing the flower twice

Wednesday,14 May

At art club, we drew one flower from a pot in the middle of the table. I began with a neat circle and added petals around it. ____1____ The real petals overlapped and did not make the regular shape I had expected.

Our tutor asked us to look for one feature before drawing again. I noticed a petal folded partly behind another. ____2____ The second sketch became less tidy but closer to the view in front of me.

My friend was sitting opposite. Her drawing showed a different arrangement. At first I thought one of us must be wrong. ____3____ We were not seeing exactly the same side of the flower.

We put both sketches beside the pot for the final discussion. The tutor did not ask us to select one as the only true picture. ____4____ I kept the first drawing too, because it showed the expectation I had brought to the task.

The receipt in the coat pocket

Saturday,17 May

I found a shop receipt in a coat pocket while helping Dad tidy. It listed a loaf, oranges and a small notebook. I thought it was rubbish and reached for the paper bin. ____1____ He recognised the date before I had read the shop name.

The receipt came from a holiday when we had stayed in a village near the sea. Dad remembered buying the notebook for me after I asked for somewhere to draw the boats. ____2____ The notebook itself was still on my shelf, full of those pictures.

We did not decide to keep every old receipt forever. Dad said this one had a particular connection we wanted to record. ____3____ The note explained why an ordinary list mattered to us, without pretending it was important to everyone.

Later, I looked through the notebook. One boat had a red sail I no longer remembered seeing. The receipt did not prove every detail of the drawing. ____4____ Different records helped us recover different parts of the same day.

The receipt came from a holiday when we had stayed in a village near the sea. Dad remembered buying the notebook for me after I asked for somewhere to draw the boats. ____2____ The notebook itself was still on my shelf, full of those pictures.

We did not decide to keep every old receipt forever. Dad said this one had a particular connection we wanted to record. ____3____ The note explained why an ordinary list mattered to us, without pretending it was important to everyone.

originalGroup.material:
Joining an ongoing class project

Joining a project after it has started can feel awkward. Other members may use names for files, parts or routines that are unfamiliar to you. ____1____ The aim is to enter the work with enough context, not pretend you already know everything.

Ask a useful first question

A specific question is easier to answer than a general request to explain the whole project. You might say, "____2____" Knowing the immediate task can give the rest of the discussion a clearer place.

Check what has been agreed

Separate decisions already made from ideas still being considered. ____3____ Otherwise, an early suggestion may be repeated as if the group had promised to carry it out.

Take a manageable part

Choose an initial task you can complete and report on. ____4____ A small agreed contribution can teach you more than silently trying to redesign everything at once.

____5____

When the task is finished, tell the group what you did, where the result is and what remains uncertain. This gives others a useful next step and makes it easier for someone else to join later.

Giving a useful comment on someone’s work

A comment can help a writer see how a draft is being read. It is less useful when it offers only a verdict with no connection to the words. ____1____ The writer needs something they can examine, not merely a label to accept or reject.

Point to a particular place

Identify the moment that produced your response. You might say, "____2____" That gives the writer a location and an account of what happened during your reading.

Distinguish response from instruction

Saying you were confused is different from requiring one particular rewrite. ____3____ The writer may find another way to address the same difficulty.

Keep the scale reasonable

One reader's reaction does not establish what everyone will feel. ____4____ This makes the comment more accurate without making it less worth hearing.

____5____

After explaining the issue, allow the writer to ask questions or describe the intended effect. You do not need to win an argument. A useful exchange can clarify a choice even when the two people still prefer different versions.
